lesson.topicTitle: Structure and functions in living organisms

specAnchors.text: describe the structure and function of the human alimentary canal, including the mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine (duodenum and ileum), large intestine (colon and rectum) and pancreas

primer.text: You have followed food from mouth to stomach already. This lesson maps the whole alimentary canal end to end — mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine — and adds the accessory organs, the liver, gall bladder and pancreas, whose secretions do much of the real chemistry along the way.

modules.title: The Canal and Its Accessory Organs
sourceHeadings: The Structure & Function of the Alimentary Canal
Alimentary canal and accessory structures table
modules.opening: The alimentary canal is one continuous tube from mouth to anus, and each region does a distinct job: the mouth ingests and breaks food up, the oesophagus delivers it, the stomach churns and acidifies, the small intestine digests and absorbs, and the large intestine dries the remains. Around it sit accessory organs whose secretions run the chemistry.
keyPoints: The canal is a continuous tube running from mouth to anus.
Each region — mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine — has a distinct function.
The liver, gall bladder and pancreas are accessory structures aiding digestion.
The small intestine carries out most digestion and absorption.
The large intestine absorbs remaining water from the undigested residue.

low.restatement: One tube, five stations, three helper organs alongside.
low.analogy: A factory line with stations and off-line supply rooms.
low.examPointer: Learn the canal's regions in order; sequence questions are common.

medium.restatement: Mechanical work happens early, chemical digestion and absorption peak in the small intestine, and water recovery ends the trip.
medium.analogy: A mine, a refinery and a drying yard on one industrial site.
medium.examPointer: Match each accessory organ to its secretion for full marks.

glossary.definition: The continuous muscular tube from mouth to anus through which food travels.
A digestive organ such as the liver or pancreas whose secretions aid the canal without food passing through it.
The semi-liquid food mass produced by churning in the stomach.
